# RETRO: PR #13186 (team 5)

## What worked
- The neutral brief plus the dependency-source scope let both reviewers go to the Qt `qv4dateobject.cpp` source. Opus built a headless Qt 6.11.2 harness (`qml6 --apptype core`) and checked the full zone matrix, which settled the engine claims without a desktop.
- The targeted cross-examination turned two Opus-only public claims into independently confirmed ones in a single Sol follow-up.

## Avoidable friction / deviations
- Coordinator: during the policy read, two parallel 50-line reads were issued twice (about 100 lines per response), over the 60-line aggregate bound. The content was read completely.
- Coordinator: the first extraction of the Opus report took the closing message instead of the SubagentHandback payload. It is preserved as `opus/extract-attempt-1-closing-message.md`, and the corrected extraction is in `opus/final-report.md`.
- Harness: the `omarchy-reviewer` subagent was blocked from writing its report file ("Subagents should return findings as text"). This conflicts with the runtime section, which says the reviewer saves reports under `opus/`. Fixture evidence writes did succeed. Suggested improvement: have the coordinator save the handback verbatim as a documented step, or allow report writes for this agent type.
- Opus reviewer (self-reported): three read-size overruns (about 55-70 lines); one partial source snapshot missing a file the test reads (a failed run, excluded); one parallel fixture edit plus init; a GUI-mode `qml6 --version` SIGABRT (run excluded); and a Qt logging sink issue fixed with `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1`. All invalid runs are preserved and excluded.
- Sol copied a Node binary from a host mise install into its fixture (hashed; no host execution). Opus downloaded the official tarball, verified by checksum only.
- Disk: `opus/` is about 904 MB (six copies of the Node binary in sealed bundles). Cleanup is left to the user or orchestrator.

## Carry forward
- For QML/JS model PRs, a headless `qml6 --apptype core` harness with `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1` gives real Qt engine evidence without a desktop slot.
- Pass the subagent report-write limitation to the orchestrator for a workflow fix.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** no production issue found. Building `monthGrid()` from `Date.UTC`, stepping by `MS_PER_DAY` and reading cells with the `getUTC*` accessors fixes the column drift in the Qt QML engine and the dropped day in V8. Ordinary months are unchanged. Head `Model.js` matched an independent integer calendar reference in every case checked: all 341 IANA zones, every month from 1970 to 2040, Sunday, Monday and Saturday week starts, under both Qt 6.11.2 and Node 26. The check covered day numbers, `inMonth`, weekend flags, the single `today` cell and ISO week numbers. The base walk mismatched in 139 zones under Qt. Five of them (Santiago, Havana, Beirut, Azores, Cairo) mismatch every year from 2025 through 2040.

```text
Qt 6.11.2 QML engine, America/Santiago, September 2026, Sunday start (row 2)
            SUN MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT
base          5   6   7   8   9  10  11    <- 5 repeated, later days one column right
head          6   7   8   9  10  11  12

Node and Qt, Pacific/Apia, December 2011, Monday start (row 5)
            MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT SUN
base         26  27  28  29  31   1   2    <- 30 dropped
head         26  27  28  29  30  31   1
```

**Verified:** `test/shell.d/clock-test.sh` passes on head (160 `ok` lines) with the ambient `TZ` set to UTC, America/Santiago, Pacific/Apia, Pacific/Kiritimati, America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Kolkata, so the `process.env.TZ` restore works. Run against the base `Model.js`, it stops at `not ok - calendar keeps a day the local zone skipped entirely`, matching the PR description.

**Optional test improvement:** the assertion `calendar leaves a Thursday in the Thursday column after a midnight jump` reads each `today` cell's own `weekday` field. That field is computed from the cell's date, not from its position in the row. In the Qt run of the base model, 24 September is drawn under FRI yet still reports `weekday: 4`, so the assertion passes on the broken code in both engines. A position check catches the drift directly:

```js
const order = calendar.weekdayOrder(0)
assert(santiago.every(week => week.days.every((day, column) => day.weekday === order[column])),
  'calendar leaves every weekday in its own column after a midnight jump')
```

The three Santiago assertions all pass on the base model under Node, as the PR description notes. Under the Node-based suite, only the two Apia assertions separate head from base. A short test comment saying so would keep the Santiago block from being read as regression coverage.

**Optional:** the new comments in `Model.js` and the test say a missing hour lands "back on the same day under Qt, forward past the next one under V8". Qt 6.11.2 also resolves Apia's missing 30 December forward to the 31st. The direction depends on the zone's offsets around the transition and on the standard offset the engine caches at startup. V8 lands Santiago on the correct day. A wording such as "engines resolve a nonexistent local time differently" would stay accurate.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of both changed files, the `Panel.qml` caller and the public qtdeclarative 6.11.2 Date implementation. `Model.js` (base and head) ran headlessly in the Qt 6.11.2 QML engine and in Node 26 across the zone, month and week-start matrix above, in an isolated sandbox with tzdata 2026c. `clock-test.sh` ran under Node. Not tested: the running bar or any Quickshell session, and the rest of the `test/shell` suite.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
